fine_lines.title: reschedule vs rebook
fine_lines.explanation_ar: reschedule تغيير موعد نفس الحدث (اجتماع أو رحلة) دون إلغائه، فقط تأجيل أو تقديم. rebook حجز جديد تماماً برقم حجز وتذكرة جديدة، لأن الحجز الأول أُلغي أو فاتك.

examples.sentence: My flight was delayed, so they rescheduled it for 5 p.m.
I missed my flight, so I had to rebook a new one.

fine_lines.explanation_en: 'Reschedule' means changing the time of the same event (a meeting or a flight) without cancelling it, just moving it earlier or later. 'Rebook' means making a completely new booking with a new booking number and ticket, because the first one was cancelled or you missed it.

fine_lines.title: accident vs incident
fine_lines.explanation_ar: incident أي حدث غير معتاد يسبب ضجة أو يعطّل اليوم، ولا يشترط وجود إصابات (مثل شجار في المطار أو ضياع حقيبة). accident حادث غير متوقع فيه أضرار أو إصابات (مثل حادث سيارة). كل accident هو incident، لكن ليس كل incident هو accident.

examples.sentence: Two people were injured in the car accident.
There was a small incident at the gate, but nobody was hurt.

fine_lines.explanation_en: An 'incident' is any unusual event that causes trouble or disturbs the day; nobody has to be hurt (like a fight at the airport or a lost bag). An 'accident' is an unexpected event with damage or injuries (like a car crash). Every accident is an incident, but not every incident is an accident.

fine_lines.title: sickness vs disease
fine_lines.explanation_ar: disease هو المرض نفسه باسمه (مثل الإنفلونزا). sickness هو حالة الشعور بالمرض أو التعب (مثل دوار البحر أو الجو).

examples.sentence: Travel sickness made him feel terrible on the bus.

fine_lines.explanation_en: A 'disease' is a specific illness with a name (like flu). 'Sickness' is the state of feeling ill or unwell (like seasickness or airsickness).

grammar.title: Action verbs vs state verbs
grammar.explanation_ar: أغلب الأفعال أفعال حركة (run, eat, travel) ويمكن استخدامها في الأزمنة المستمرة. لكن أفعال الحالة تصف شعوراً أو تفكيراً أو امتلاكاً، وليس فيها حركة تراها، لذلك لا نضيف لها ing عادة. من أشهرها: need, want, like, love, hate, know, believe, own, have (يمتلك).
examples: I need a refund. (not: I am needing)
I know the answer. (not: I am knowing)
I have travel insurance. (not: I am having)
grammar.explanation_en: Most verbs are action verbs (run, eat, travel) and can be used in continuous tenses. But state verbs describe a feeling, a thought or owning something, with no action you can see, so we usually don't add -ing to them. Common ones: need, want, like, love, hate, know, believe, own, have (meaning to own).
